notes.title: Metroid Dread Update: Accidentally fixed some menu bugs
notes.content:
I upgraded Heart Lock's project files to a newer Unity version, which unintentionally fixed the menu bugs.

I've titled this the "Metroid Dread Update" because it will be the last update I put out before Metroid Dread releases.

I spent more time editing the spooky cover art for this update than the time it took to publish the game files lol.

notes.title: v1.0.2 - Revised one of the tweaks
notes.content:
[h1]- Spell damage is back to normal![/h1]
[h1]- For two-ish weeks, all players are BEEFIER![/h1]

I published that last update with haste (got worried about players getting one-shotted). I played a bit yesterday, and got annoyed at how long thing were taking to kill, so I bumped spell damage back up the original values.

Now, about that damage resistance. Players on older versions start their game with 10 health, resulting in a one-hit-death from literally everything in the game. Moving forward, players will start with 20 health (hint: if you need more health, there's a Health Booster very close to the Pillow Fort). To accommodate for players on older versions that start with only 10 health, I've added a damage resistance modifier that prevents players from getting one-hit-deaths.

Suggestion! If you are not very far in the game, find "Reset Save File" in the "Abilities & Modifiers" tab. Hitting this button will put your base health up to 20 points.

[b]This is a temporary fix.[/b] I will be removing this in a 1-2 weeks to give players some time to catch up and get their base health above 10 points. This damage resistance tweak makes late-game players very tanky, so take advantage of this while you can.

notes.title: v1.0.2 - Some Balancing Tweaks
notes.content:
[b]All enemies drop more dust![/b]

- All critters no longer cast Shade spells (the dark blob that is difficult to see). These spells were originally designed in Mind Lock, of which has much brighter backgrounds. 
- To replace Shade spell, toasters now cast Glow spells.
- Removed a toaster at the beginning of the level. 
- Added elemental barrier at beginning of the game to encourage players to test out different spells before fighting their first enemy.
- Modified base player stats. Previously, new players could die in one hit. This was not intentional. You will notice the effect when resetting your save file. As a courtesy, ALL spells' base damage has been reduced temporarily.
- We are actively fixing a bug in the music player, where Pillow Fort theme songs would (unintentionally) play during exploration. If you encounter issues with music, either rest at a Pillow Fort or use the "Play Next Song" button in your "Settings & Music" menu.

notes.title: Heart Lock Is Live! And It's Free!
notes.content:
Have fun playing! For a little background, this project was inspired as a result of playing Super Metroid over the summer, which resulted going down a deep rabbit hole discovering many fan creations in the Super Metroid community. While you don't use guns on an alien planet, I hope that I have re-created a experience that elicits similar wonder and emotions while playing Super Metroid (and any other like it).
